text:
noah: Starting bring-up for customer Elysian LoRA v1 on int8. Running a tight quick-eval (invoices + table sums).

jia: nice. did you run tokenizer alignment and delta? Elysian had mixed UTF-8 currency glyphs before.

noah: ran align + delta and applied remap. cmd: 
```
python infra/token_align.py --src models/base-elysian/tokenizer.json --dst customers/elysian/tokenizer.json --out /tmp/ely_token_map.json
python infra/token_delta.py --base models/base-elysian/tokenizer.json --target customers/elysian/tokenizer.json --out /tmp/ely_delta.txt
```

ci-bot: queued: quick-eval/1799123456-elysian-int8 (priority: high) :rocket:

omari: quick look at first 10 prompts: totals look OK but one case produced a leading zero-pad and one produced a weird prefix "�-" before the amount.

lina: customer requires strict amount formatting. any prefix or null char is a blocker for billing.

noah: interesting. initial quant config used our default int8 suggestion. trying a couple runtime knobs: 
```
quant: int8
per_channel: true
group_size: 128
act_order: symmetric
kv_cache_prefill: false
```
I'll also try raj's token-bytefix branch (token-fix/elysian-byte-order) that adjusts decode byte order for unusual multi-byte currency glyphs.

ci-bot: quick-eval started -> quick-eval/1799123456-elysian-int8: 0/40 complete.

noah: running eval script: 
```
python tools/run_quick_eval.py --model base-elysian --lora customers/elysian/elysian-lora-v1 --quant int8 --prompts eval_packs/elysian_invoices_small.json --out /tmp/ely_eval.json --batch-size 3
```

noah: mid-run (20/40): dumped raw tokens for failing sample #6. looks like decode emitted a null byte before sign for certain currency glyphs. raw bytes: [0x24, 0x00, 0x2D, ...] decoded -> "�-$21.49". fp16 baseline decodes to "$21.49".

jia: null byte suggests a byte-order or decode table mismatch, maybe introduced during quant kernel packing. token-fix branch likely relevant. can you attach raw logits and token ids for that case?

noah: attached logs snippet for sample 6 in artifacts. quick summary so far: 40 prompts total, 38 pass, 2 failures (one null prefix, one swapped cents). p95 latency +8% vs fp16, cost ~-42%. failing snippet:
```
input: "Items: $12.99, $3.50. Total?"
fp16_expected: "$21.49"
int8_output: "�-$21.49"  # leading null then sign
```

omari: swapped cents case might be token split/merge ordering ("$21.49" -> ["$21", ".49"] then join reversed). but the null prefix smells like a decode table indexing issue.

lina: customer flagged this as critical. they'd accept a 1-week canary only if invoice endpoints remain on fp16. please include that in rollout plan.

noah: plan: 1) rerun with token-fix/elysian-byte-order + kv_cache_prefill=false; 2) if fixes both cases, create canary (10% traffic) with invoice route pinned to int8 only after an additional verification run; otherwise keep invoice route on fp16 with int8 for other routes; 3) upload eval JSON + failing samples to infra/rollouts/1799123456.

jia: also add a tiny unit test that asserts no control chars in decoded outputs for currency prompts. good regression coverage.

ci-bot: quick-eval complete: 40/40. summary: 38 OK, 2 regressions (null prefix, cents-order). artifacts: /ci/artifacts/quick-eval/1799123456/summary.json :white_check_mark:

noah: opening infra/rollouts/1799123456 with artifacts and PR link to token-fix. tagging @lina for CS. will follow up with the canary plan once rerun finishes.

lina: drafting customer note. please ping when rerun passes or if we decide to keep invoice route on fp16. :memo:

omari: filing a follow-up bug to trace how decode table gets a null entry during int8 kernel packing. marking as P0 for inference correctness.
